page: Microsoft Azure D48ads_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and x86_64 architecture. The server is configured with 48 dedicated vCPUs derived from 24 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at 3.7 GHz. System memory capacity totals 192.0 GB, adhering to a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory balance with 4.0 GB allocated per vCPU. Hardware features include 2835 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage. The processor incorporates 32 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and hardware instruction support for AVX-512 (f, vnni, and bf16) alongside cryptographic extensions like VAES and SHA-NI. No discrete GPUs are provided.

Benchmark results show top-tier computational performance across multi-threaded and single-threaded synthetic tests. The system achieves a multi-core stress-ng score of 73828.07 and a PassMark CPU score of 62724.38, placing it in the top 25% of evaluated systems. High-intensity tasks such as software compilation in Clang (47221.0) and PassMark database operations (22127.37) reflect strong instruction throughput. In-memory processing metrics show Redis SET operations reaching 63.99 million operations per second, supported by fast small-block cached memory bandwidth of 3648.63 GB/sec. Uncached large-block read and write bandwidth remain moderate at 116.44 GB/sec and 83.34 GB/sec, respectively.

Without hardware acceleration, large language model generation drops significantly on larger architectures, producing 2.52 tokens per second on a 70B model, whereas smaller 135M models achieve 330.06 tokens per second. The server offers cost-effective hardware utilization for organizations requiring balanced memory, strong compute throughput, and high local I/O capacity on a single virtual host. It is structurally suited for relational databases, Redis caching layers, continuous integration build clusters, and data processing pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure D48ads_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 48 vCPUs across 24 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz. The system provides 192.0 GB of RAM alongside 2835 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage on the x86_64 architecture under Microsoft Hyper-V. Lacking discrete GPUs, the configuration relies on AVX-512 and hardware cryptographic instructions for accelerated processing. Benchmark evaluations place both single-core and multi-core CPU metrics in the upper quartile, highlighted by high compilation and database operation results, as well as 63.99 million Redis SET operations per second. However, uncached memory bandwidth settles in the middle tier, and large-scale model inference is constrained by CPU-only execution. The server is well configured for enterprise application hosting, relational databases, software build pipelines, and caching deployments needing high local disk throughput.
